## Which Ada Tours trips visit the San Blas Islands?

The [San Blas Islands](/panama/place/san-blas-islands/) lie in the Caribbean Sea off the northeastern coast of [Panama](/panama/), within Guna Yala. Small islands, sandy beaches, coral reefs and Guna settlements give the archipelago its distinctive atmosphere. Some travelers come for a beach visit; others choose a multi-day sailing journey to reach more remote islands. Even when the destination is the same, these are different types of travel.

We offer {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} with San Blas in the core itinerary. The best way to choose is to compare how much time you spend on the islands themselves and where you sleep. The live tour table shows the full routes and durations.

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_source_panama_2024,tour_source_ostrova_san_blas_na_yakhte_lyuks_klassa}}

| Format | San Blas experience |
|---|---|
| Panama, 16 days | Day trip from the capital |
| Yacht voyage, 8 days | Several island anchorages and nights aboard |

### The extended Panama journey: one day on the Caribbean islands

The [16-day Panama tour](/panama/tour/panama-2024/) visits San Blas on day four. Hotel departure is scheduled for **05:00**, with a return in the evening. It is one Caribbean chapter of a wider trip, with other days devoted to [Panama City](/panama/place/panama-city/), [Chagres National Park](/panama/place/chagres-national-park/), historical coastal fortifications, [Boca Chica](/panama/place/boca-chica/), [Boquete](/panama/place/boquete/) and [Bocas del Toro](/panama/place/bocas-del-toro/).

This is a good option for exploring many parts of Panama in one journey. San Blas is a single day of beaches and turquoise water, followed by further travel around the country. **This itinerary does not include overnight stays on the islands**: the published program specifies a return to the hotel after the excursion.

The details of the separate yacht tour must not be attributed to this day trip. Remote reefs, overnight sailing and multiple island stops belong to the dedicated marine itinerary, not the excursion from the capital.

### The yacht journey: San Blas as the main purpose of the trip

The [8-day San Blas luxury yacht tour](/panama/tour/panama-san-blas-luxury-yacht/) centers on sailing. The first stage starts near [Flamenco Island](/panama/place/flamenco-island/), after which the yacht crosses the [Panama Canal](/panama/place/panama-canal/) and reaches the Caribbean coast through [Shelter Bay](/panama/place/shelter-bay/). The remainder focuses on the islands of Guna Yala.

The published schedule lists [El Porvenir](/panama/place/el-porvenir-island/), [Coco Bandero](/panama/place/coco-bandero-island/), the [Holandes Cays](/panama/place/holandes-cays/), [Isla Perro](/panama/place/isla-perro/) and [Turtle Island](/panama/place/turtle-island/) in sequence. Swimming, snorkeling, island walks and marine-life observation feature on different days. Yacht accommodation and island excursions are included, while international flights are listed separately.

Unlike the 16-day land tour, **the sea sets the pace and order of this trip**. The islands are its main stages. Check the precise included services, accommodation on board and Panama Canal transit conditions for the selected voyage. A VIP label alone does not guarantee that every island activity is private.

## Choosing between a day trip and a cruise

For a first introduction to Panama, a longer land itinerary with one day at San Blas is often more convenient. It combines the shores of two oceans, a mountain region and protected natural areas. There are more journeys between contrasting landscapes, and less time at each island stop.

The yacht trip suits travelers who want to discover a series of islands. After transiting the canal, the journey follows Caribbean bays, anchorages and reefs. It is for guests who enjoy sleeping several nights on board and accept that sailing conditions, transitions and the timetable depend on the sea.

A third possibility is spending several nights on the islands but staying ashore. Neither of the two listed programs includes that standalone accommodation option. It cannot be assumed to form part of the yacht voyage or the 16-day tour. See the separate [San Blas destination page](/panama/place/san-blas-islands/) to explore the archipelago.

## Guna Yala: local rules and travel logistics

San Blas belongs to the autonomous territory of the Indigenous Guna community. Visiting means respecting local regulations, residents and traditions. The Guna's distinctive *mola* textile appliqués are particularly important in local culture; tourism and marine livelihoods support many families.

The usual road-and-boat route from [Panama City](/panama/place/panama-city/) travels to Cartí port and then by boat to the chosen island. Panama's tourism authority suggests about **three hours by four-wheel-drive vehicle**; the boat journey depends on the final destination. Local fees and rules apply to entering the territory, using boats and visiting islands. **The actual transfer arrangements and prepaid charges must be checked against the chosen tour:** general Guna Yala visiting information does not replace Ada Tours' terms.

The yacht journey has different logistics. The vessel arrives via the [Panama Canal](/panama/place/panama-canal/) and [Shelter Bay](/panama/place/shelter-bay/), then sails between island anchorages. That is why the prices and durations cannot be compared solely by counting days in the archipelago: transport and accommodation work quite differently.

Ask where photography is permitted in communities and which places welcome visitors. Buying local crafts and taking agreed excursions can be a respectful way to learn about living Guna culture.

## Weather and packing

Panama's Caribbean coast has a generally drier period from December to April and a wetter remainder of the year. The word “dry” alone does not predict a comfortable passage: winds and rougher water can occur in the dry season. Rain is more common in the greener months, though calm spells at sea are still possible. **The crew decides whether to sail based on the forecast and actual marine conditions**, not a seasonal chart.

For a day trip, pack light clothes, a hat, sun protection, a waterproof bag for documents and a dry change of clothes. For sailing, add non-slip shoes, a windproof layer and compact luggage. Snorkeling or scuba activities require confirmation of the exact equipment and conditions of the chosen itinerary; the presence of reefs does not automatically mean paid diving is included.

Compare the first departure time, overnight arrangements, type of sea passages and planned anchorages. These practical details shape the experience of San Blas more than a generic description of “Caribbean islands.”

## Frequently asked questions

### Can you see San Blas in one day?

Yes. The [16-day Panama tour](/panama/tour/panama-2024/) includes one dedicated day with an early departure from the capital and a return in the evening. This introduces the islands as part of a longer land journey.

### Which tours include overnight stays on a yacht?

The [8-day sailing itinerary](/panama/tour/panama-san-blas-luxury-yacht/) includes accommodation aboard the yacht. The 16-day tour's day trip does not involve overnight stays on the islands or on a yacht.

### What is included in the yacht trip?

The published inclusions specify yacht accommodation and island excursions. International flights are excluded. Meals, the precise vessel and private services must be checked in the specific offer; the word VIP cannot establish them.

### Are Holandes and Isla Perro different from San Blas as a whole?

Yes. The [Holandes Cays](/panama/place/holandes-cays/) are a particular group of reef islands, while [Isla Perro](/panama/place/isla-perro/) is one island. Both belong to the larger archipelago. A generic visit to San Blas does not guarantee a stop at each.

### How can I combine San Blas with other regions of Panama?

If islands and mountains both appeal, the [16-day itinerary](/panama/tour/panama-2024/) continues after its Caribbean excursions to Pacific [Boca Chica](/panama/place/boca-chica/), the coffee-growing region of [Boquete](/panama/place/boquete/) and [Bocas del Toro](/panama/place/bocas-del-toro/). See the full [Panama tours catalog](/panama/tour/) for more options.

## San Lorenzo Fortress: a stronghold above the mouth of the Chagres River

**San Lorenzo** is a historic fortress on the Caribbean coast of [Panama](/panama/), near the mouth of the [Chagres River](/panama/place/chagres-river/). Its surviving stone walls and bastions stand above the sea amid tropical vegetation. Even without a detailed account of the battles, it is easy to see why the fortress was built here: the defenses overlooked the river entrance, once a vital route across the Isthmus of Panama.

San Lorenzo and the fortifications of [Portobelo](/panama/place/portobelo/) have shared UNESCO World Heritage status since **1980**. They form one protected heritage listing but occupy two distinct locations, and travel between them must be planned.

## How the fortress protected trade routes

In the colonial era, goods moved across Panama between the Pacific and the Caribbean. The Chagres River and overland stretches of the isthmus were crucial to this traffic, so the river mouth had to be protected. The Spanish Crown built Caribbean-side fortresses to monitor approaching vessels and repel attacks.

The earliest defenses date to the transition between the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries, with rebuilding in later centuries. The visible remains represent several phases of military architecture. This is not a castle with fully intact rooms: the main attractions are the layout of the fortifications, the walls, artillery positions and views of the river mouth.

UNESCO describes San Lorenzo and Portobelo as monuments of seventeenth- and eighteenth-century Spanish military architecture linked to transatlantic commerce.

## What to look for on the site

The surviving walls, bastions and gun positions help visitors imagine how defenders moved and how artillery was arranged. The view down to the mouth of the Chagres is particularly striking: the fortress was guarding the entrance to a major transport route, not an arbitrary stretch of coastline.

Look at the position of the defenses above the sea, surviving stonework and the contrast with the surrounding tropical forest. Access to individual areas depends on current heritage-protection rules. Some parts may close for restoration or safety.

Rain can make the old stones slippery. Wear closed shoes, carry water and sun protection, and allow enough time to explore.

## Arranging a visit from Panama City

San Lorenzo is on the Caribbean side of the isthmus, away from central [Panama City](/panama/place/panama-city/). Visiting by car involves a drive toward the coast and a local approach to the fort. It is not convenient to treat it as a short walk after visiting a city museum.

One rewarding combination is San Lorenzo and the [Agua Clara Locks](/panama/place/agua-clara-locks/). This allows you to compare the colonial Chagres transport system with the modern [Panama Canal](/panama/place/panama-canal/). Portobelo tells a related story but requires a separate drive.

| Site | What it reveals |
|---|---|
| San Lorenzo | Defense of the river mouth |
| Agua Clara | The modern canal |
| [Portobelo](/panama/place/portobelo/) | Caribbean fortifications |

## Which Ada Tours trips include the fortress?

The [4-day Panama itinerary](/panama/tour/panama-city-anton-valley-san-lorenzo/) combines Panama City, [Antón Valley](/panama/place/el-valle-de-anton/) and San Lorenzo. The fortress and Agua Clara Locks are visited on the same day. The excursion is guided in Russian; lunch that day is not included in the excursion price.

When comparing trips, check whether transfers, admission tickets and guiding specifically at this historic site are included. See [Panama cultural and historical tours](/interests/culture-and-history/tours/panama/) for a wider selection.

## What to confirm before departure

Opening hours and access to some areas may change due to restoration or natural conditions, so visiting times should be agreed shortly before the trip. An open-air stone fortress differs from a museum: there is little shelter from sun or rain, and uneven surfaces require care.

San Lorenzo suits travelers interested in maritime trade, fortifications and the connection between Panama's geography and its economic past.

## Frequently asked questions about San Lorenzo

### Why is San Lorenzo on the UNESCO list?

The fortress is part of Panama's historic Caribbean-coast defenses together with Portobelo. It illustrates the Spanish system built to protect trading routes.

### Is it the same site as the Portobelo forts?

No. San Lorenzo stands at the mouth of the Chagres; Portobelo is a separate complex on the Caribbean coast.

### Can you visit the fortress and the Panama Canal locks on the same trip?

Yes. This combination is included in Ada Tours' current four-day itinerary.

## Which Ada Tours trips visit San Lorenzo Fortress?

[San Lorenzo Fortress](/panama/place/san-lorenzo-fort/) stands at the mouth of the Chagres River on the Caribbean side of [Panama](/panama/). The Spanish built fortifications here to defend the route that carried goods and valuables across the isthmus. Old bastions, stone walls and the sea view explain the fort's role in colonial trade.

Today San Lorenzo features on trips that combine a historical visit with the [Panama Canal](/panama/place/panama-canal/). We offer {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} with the fortress included in the main route. Their durations and onward stops differ, so compare the entire sequence before choosing.

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_source_panama_panama_siti_dolina_anton_krepost_san_lorenso,tour_source_panama_2024}}

| Itinerary | Main sights alongside the fort |
|---|---|
| Panama, 4 days | San Lorenzo and Agua Clara Locks |
| Panama, 16 days | San Lorenzo and Portobelo forts |

### Panama in four days: fortress, canal and Antón Valley

The [short Panama tour](/panama/tour/panama-city-anton-valley-san-lorenzo/) begins in [Panama City](/panama/place/panama-city/). One day focuses on the volcanic [El Valle de Antón](/panama/place/el-valle-de-anton/); day three is for San Lorenzo and the [Agua Clara Locks](/panama/place/agua-clara-locks/). Departure toward the Caribbean coast is scheduled for **08:00**.

After the fortress, the trip continues to the Atlantic-side locks. From the Agua Clara viewpoint, visitors can watch large ships moving and see Gatun Lake, before returning to the capital. The following day brings a tour of Panama City and its historic districts.

This is the compact option: **four days, three nights, private transportation and a Russian-language tour of the fortress and locks**. Confirmed inclusions also cover accommodation with breakfast, transfers, an excursion to Antón Valley and city sightseeing. Lunch during the San Lorenzo excursion is specifically excluded.

The short route works well for travelers who value a mix of colonial history, canal engineering and natural scenery over an extended beach or mountain holiday.

### Panama in 16 days: historic forts on a longer journey

The [16-day Panama itinerary](/panama/tour/panama-2024/) includes San Lorenzo on day five. Travelers first explore the capital, the canal, [Chagres National Park](/panama/place/chagres-national-park/) and the [San Blas Islands](/panama/place/san-blas-islands/). The next day is devoted to Caribbean forts: from San Lorenzo, the route continues to [Portobelo](/panama/place/portobelo/), where colonial defenses and historic buildings survive.

This day introduces **the wider Spanish defensive system on Panama's Caribbean shore**, not only one fortress. In Portobelo, visits include San Jerónimo, Santiago de la Gloria, San Fernando and the town's historic buildings. The exact visiting order follows the published itinerary.

The trip then continues to Pacific [Boca Chica](/panama/place/boca-chica/), the mountains of [Boquete](/panama/place/boquete/) and the Caribbean islands of [Bocas del Toro](/panama/place/bocas-del-toro/). This is suitable for travelers seeking both forts and the country's natural variety. Unlike the four-day option, San Lorenzo is just one substantial stage in a long journey.

## San Lorenzo and Portobelo: why visit both?

[San Lorenzo](/panama/place/san-lorenzo-fort/) is at the mouth of the [Chagres River](/panama/place/chagres-river/), while [Portobelo](/panama/place/portobelo/) lies farther east in its own Caribbean bay. Both defended trade across the isthmus but controlled different stretches of coast and distinct routes. Seeing the two complexes together gives a fuller picture of colonial Panama.

The San Lorenzo and Portobelo fortifications were inscribed together on the UNESCO World Heritage List in **1980**. Their historical elements date mainly from the sixteenth through eighteenth centuries, reflecting evolving defense technology in a tropical climate. The site was added to the List of World Heritage in Danger in **2012**, and a UNESCO decision in **2026** retained that status because of ongoing conservation concerns. **Protection status does not automatically prohibit visits**, but restoration and access to particular areas must be considered when choosing dates.

For two fortification complexes in a single excursion day, choose the [16-day itinerary](/panama/tour/panama-2024/), which includes both San Lorenzo and Portobelo. The [four-day tour](/panama/tour/panama-city-anton-valley-san-lorenzo/) visits Agua Clara after the fortress; it does not advertise a separate Portobelo fort tour.

## The fortress and Agua Clara: colonial history beside modern engineering

The [Agua Clara Locks](/panama/place/agua-clara-locks/) belong to the expanded Panama Canal, commissioned in **2016**. They allow Neopanamax-class vessels to transit on the Atlantic side. Visiting the fort and locks in one day reveals two eras of the isthmus: defense of colonial trade and modern shipping logistics.

The short itinerary combines these places in one Russian-language excursion. Ship movements determine when vessels can actually be seen from the locks' observation area; even at the viewpoint, a passage cannot be guaranteed for a specific minute. The official Agua Clara visitor center receives tourists, but hours, admission rules and access can change. Check tickets against the chosen package: the four-day offer includes Panama Canal admission, while lunches on certain excursion days are excluded.

For independent travelers this is also a reason to allow enough time: a historic fortress and working locks both involve driving, sightseeing and possibly waiting to observe shipping. Adding unrelated stops without adjusting the program would be unwise.

## Planning the visit

Both itineraries start from [Panama City](/panama/place/panama-city/), while San Lorenzo is on the Caribbean side of the canal. The journey crosses areas of humid tropical climate. At the fort, exposed stonework, uneven surfaces and limited shade call for closed walking shoes, water and sun protection. A light waterproof jacket is useful in the rainy season.

**Departure times and neighboring stops already differ between the two tours.** The four-day itinerary specifies an **08:00** departure and a return to the capital after Agua Clara. The 16-day route likewise starts its fort excursion in the morning but goes onward to Portobelo. Neither tour is simply a shortened copy of the other.

Consider whether you want a dedicated historical day, a visit to the locks and Russian-language guiding. For a broader introduction to Panama's culture, explore [Panama cultural tours](/interests/culture-and-history/tours/panama/) and the full [Panama tour catalog](/panama/tour/).

## Frequently asked questions

### Which Ada Tours trips include San Lorenzo?

The fortress appears in the [four-day Antón Valley and Agua Clara itinerary](/panama/tour/panama-city-anton-valley-san-lorenzo/) and the [16-day Panama journey](/panama/tour/panama-2024/). In the first, it is combined with canal locks; in the second, with Portobelo's historic forts.

### How much time is allocated to San Lorenzo?

In both programs, the fortress is one stop on an excursion day rather than a multi-day stay. The exact walking time at the monument is not specified separately and cannot be inferred from the total tour duration.

### Can the fort and Panama Canal be visited together?

Yes. The [four-day tour](/panama/tour/panama-city-anton-valley-san-lorenzo/) visits the [Agua Clara Locks](/panama/place/agua-clara-locks/) after San Lorenzo, on the Caribbean side of the canal.

### Which itinerary is best for the history of colonial Panama?

For multiple forts, the [16-day tour](/panama/tour/panama-2024/) covers San Lorenzo and [Portobelo](/panama/place/portobelo/). For a short trip combining the capital, a volcanic valley and working locks, choose the [four-day program](/panama/tour/panama-city-anton-valley-san-lorenzo/).

### Is lunch included in the fortress excursion?

On the four-day tour, lunch during the San Lorenzo and Agua Clara outing is explicitly charged separately. For the 16-day tour, consult its own inclusions and exclusions instead of applying the short program's terms.

## Shelter Bay: a yacht stop at the Caribbean entrance to the Panama Canal

Shelter Bay is a protected bay with a marina on Panama's Caribbean side, close to the Atlantic entrance to the [Panama Canal](/panama/place/panama-canal/). Yachts stop here after transiting the canal to berth and prepare for their next passages. For travelers, Shelter Bay matters primarily as part of a maritime route: it is a place where one of Panama's great engineering projects meets the everyday world of small vessels.

This is not a typical beach resort. The main sights are docks, yachts, sheltered water and the green shoreline nearby. If you want to spend a day on white sand and swim among corals, the later island stops in [San Blas](/panama/place/san-blas-islands/) are a better fit.

## Where Shelter Bay is located

The bay lies near the former Fort Sherman base, on the western side of Limón Bay close to Colón. The marina is sheltered by structures near the Panama Canal entrance. That matters: vessels can stop in protected water close to one of the region's busiest shipping passages.

According to Shelter Bay Marina's official information, the marina serves yachts and other recreational vessels and offers berths and technical facilities. Availability, requirements for a specific vessel and services must be checked directly against the marina and the planned passage. For a charter guest, Shelter Bay is usually a programmed stop rather than a separate berth to book personally.

The forests of San Lorenzo lie nearby. The coast offers a striking contrast between tropical forest and harbor infrastructure, although a forest excursion requires extra time and is not automatically included in a yacht's stop.

## Why yachts stop at Shelter Bay

### After transiting the Panama Canal

A vessel passing through the canal from the Pacific reaches the Caribbean entrance. Shelter Bay provides a convenient place to finish that stage, berth and prepare for the onward passage. In our [Ada Tours San Blas yacht journey](/panama/tour/panama-san-blas-luxury-yacht/), the transit takes a full stage: after departing from [Flamenco Island](/panama/place/flamenco-island/), the yacht crosses the canal with a Panamanian pilot and arrives at Shelter Bay.

For guests, this provides the rare experience of seeing the locks not just from the shore but aboard a vessel crossing between oceans. Canal transit depends on shipping schedules, Panama Canal Authority rules and actual operating conditions. It is not an ordinary boat ride with an unchangeable departure time.

### Before sailing into the Caribbean

After berthing, a route can continue along the Caribbean shore toward Guna Yala's islands. In our yacht voyage, the San Blas section follows Shelter Bay: El Porvenir, [Coco Bandero](/panama/place/coco-bandero-island/), the [Holandes Cays](/panama/place/holandes-cays/), [Isla Perro](/panama/place/isla-perro/) and [Turtle Island](/panama/place/turtle-island/).

The journey from marina to islands is different from the canal transit. First come engineering and navigation; next come reefs, small island anchorages and time in the water. This explains why Shelter Bay is an important stop on one continuous marine itinerary.

### Technical services and crew comfort

Shelter Bay Marina lists berthing, provisioning and vessel-maintenance services. For the captain and crew, these are practical facilities for handling yacht operations before another leg. For passengers, the stop offers a calmer interlude after a busy day on the canal.

Actual maintenance, catering, onshore accommodation and other services must not be treated as part of the tourist package merely because the marina provides them. What is included depends on the confirmed yacht-charter terms.

## Shelter Bay, the Panama Canal and San Blas: different stages

| Place | Main purpose |
|---|---|
| [Panama Canal](/panama/place/panama-canal/) | Transit between oceans and locks |
| Shelter Bay | Caribbean yacht stop after the canal |
| [San Blas](/panama/place/san-blas-islands/) | Islands, reefs and seaside recreation |

For a short trip, decide what matters more: making the canal passage aboard a vessel or spending longer on the islands. Someone chiefly interested in how the locks work might prefer a land-based canal excursion. Snorkeling enthusiasts may prefer extra island time, with Shelter Bay serving as a logistical link.

Preparation differs too. Canal transit calls for arranged documents and a vessel schedule; island days call for attention to weather at sea, sun protection and swimming safety.

## What to arrange before the stop

Berthing and canal passage are coordinated according to yacht type, permits, draft, arrival time and navigation conditions. The marina's official guidance calls for contact with port services when approaching, but passengers do not need to handle radio communications personally. The captain and vessel-support professionals take care of that.

When choosing the [Panama yacht route](/panama/tour/panama-san-blas-luxury-yacht/), ask which days are spent at sea, when going ashore is possible and whether there is flexibility for changes to the canal schedule. Shelter Bay helps link the canal with the islands into one journey, but it replaces neither a beach stop nor a complete excursion to the coast's historical sites.

## Frequently asked questions about Shelter Bay

### Is Shelter Bay on the Pacific or the Caribbean?

On Panama's Caribbean, or Atlantic, side, close to the canal entrance near Colón.

### Can travelers visit Shelter Bay during a Panama Canal transit?

It depends on the vessel's route and stopping point. The [Ada Tours yacht program](/panama/tour/panama-san-blas-luxury-yacht/) specifically includes arrival at Shelter Bay after crossing the canal.

### Are there beaches to relax on at Shelter Bay?

The place is chiefly known for its marina and protected yacht moorings. The following stage, the [San Blas Islands](/panama/place/san-blas-islands/), is where the tour includes sandy island stops.

### Does a yacht guest need to reserve a berth personally?

Charter passengers arrange the trip with their organizer. The vessel's operator manages marina access and berthing; a particular berth and services depend on confirmation from the marina.

## Which Ada Tours trip visits Shelter Bay?

[Shelter Bay](/panama/place/shelter-bay/) is on the Caribbean side of the [Panama Canal](/panama/place/panama-canal/). Its yacht marina welcomes vessels arriving after a passage from the Pacific to the Caribbean. For sailors, this is an important intermediate stop: the canal is behind them, and Caribbean passages and island anchorages lie ahead.

Our catalog includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} with Shelter Bay on the main itinerary. This is the [eight-day yacht voyage through the Panama Canal to San Blas](/panama/tour/panama-san-blas-luxury-yacht/). The bay appears on **day two**. It is **a stop on a continuous sailing journey**, not a separate beach resort with several hotel nights.

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_source_ostrova_san_blas_na_yakhte_lyuks_klassa}}

The main reason to choose this tour is the combination of sailing through the canal and staying at several islands. The itinerary does not automatically include independent accommodation at the marina or a separate holiday in the bay. Its confirmed format is a yacht voyage with island excursions and nights aboard.

## Why the route starts on the Pacific and passes through a Caribbean bay

On day one, travelers arrive in Panama. After a welcome, a transfer brings them to the yacht near [Flamenco Island](/panama/place/flamenco-island/) on the Pacific side. Guests meet the crew, settle into their cabins and enjoy welcome drinks and a dinner prepared by the yacht's chef.

On day two, a Panamanian pilot joins the crew for the passage through the [Panama Canal](/panama/place/panama-canal/). After crossing the isthmus, the yacht reaches the Caribbean side and arrives at Shelter Bay. The passage vividly illustrates Panama's geography: within one sailing stage, the vessel passes between two ocean basins, and the rest of the journey continues along the Caribbean coast.

One important detail: **canal transit is subject to shipping schedules and Panama Canal Authority regulations**. The exact entrance time, transit order and technical arrangements depend on permissions, vessel class and operating conditions. The program confirms the crossing, not a precise minute at which the yacht will pass a lock or a promise of no waiting.

Shelter Bay connects the canal to the [San Blas Islands](/panama/place/san-blas-islands/). Watching other yachts and marina activity adds to the marine experience, but the stop itself does not imply included land excursions or accommodation ashore.

## Where the yacht sails after Shelter Bay

After the Caribbean stop, the yacht continues east toward Guna Yala. The itinerary lists a sequence of island anchorages. Each stop has its own purpose, so it is more useful to examine the complete route than just the broad name “San Blas.”

### El Porvenir: the start of the island section

On day three, the yacht travels to [El Porvenir Island](/panama/place/el-porvenir-island/). During the stop, the captain handles immigration documents and cruise permits. While these formalities are completed, guests can remain on board or walk on the island within the agreed stop.

This illustrates the role of Shelter Bay: stopping near the Caribbean entrance to the canal and later entering Guna Yala are separate phases of sailing logistics. Island entry involves its own arrangements and rules, not just distance across the water.

### Coco Bandero and Holandes: reefs and anchorages

The next anchorage is [Coco Bandero Island](/panama/place/coco-bandero-island/), surrounded by shallow reefs. The tour includes swimming and exploring the underwater world, including snorkeling. This is a major advantage of traveling by yacht: guests can visit several islands connected by marine passages.

The route then reaches the [Holandes Cays](/panama/place/holandes-cays/) for island and reef stops. Fishing, underwater swimming and beach relaxation are also mentioned. The exact availability and inclusion of each activity follow the tour's actual terms: a reef alone does not guarantee organized scuba dives, equipment rental or a private instructor.

### Isla Perro and Turtle Island

Day six features [Isla Perro](/panama/place/isla-perro/), known for shallow water and an underwater object visible to snorkelers. On day seven, the tour visits [Turtle Island](/panama/place/turtle-island/) for time on the beach and a chance to experience island nature.

These stops show why Shelter Bay is not the journey's main beach destination. After the marina, the yacht spends much of the trip among islands. On day eight, the cruise ends, with a return to Panama by small aircraft.

## Shelter Bay Marina: what matters to guests and what is vessel operations

Shelter Bay is a yacht marina at the Caribbean approach to the Panama Canal. Its shore facilities serve boats preparing to transit or those that have just completed the passage. Guests may observe marina life: moored yachts, crew activity and how sea routes connect to shore services.

**Availability at the marina does not mean a service is included in the Ada Tours price.** Yacht repairs and maintenance, individual land trips, additional transport and hotel stays do not become part of the package merely because they are offered nearby. The published yacht tour lists accommodation aboard and island excursions, with international flights explicitly excluded.

The historic [San Lorenzo Fortress](/panama/place/san-lorenzo-fort/) lies not far from the Caribbean canal entrance. It is a separate cultural attraction, but **the stop at Shelter Bay on this yacht trip does not include a visit to the fortress**. Those who want to explore its fortifications should look at the [San Lorenzo tours catalog](/panama/place/san-lorenzo-fort/tour/), rather than assume an extra excursion from the marina.

## Documents and conditions affecting the passage

For a small vessel, transit through the Panama Canal requires compliance with special regulations: arranging a passage, required assistance and the assigned shipping schedule. Procedures vary by yacht specifications. A pilot is explicitly listed in this Ada Tours itinerary, but that is a description of this voyage, not a universal rule for every yacht.

Continuing toward the Guna Yala islands brings local rules as well. The territory is governed by Indigenous Guna communities, and vessels entering its waters or visiting islands must follow their permits and customs. Our itinerary provides for the captain to complete formalities at El Porvenir. This does not exempt passengers automatically from any individual document requirements: passports, the right to enter Panama and other conditions depend on citizenship and the actual journey.

Before sailing, guests should clarify how they reach the yacht, what happens if the canal transit time changes and how strong winds might affect island visits. These are essential questions for a yacht itinerary, more important than optional amenities at the marina.

## When to sail from the canal toward the Caribbean islands

Panama's Caribbean coast is warm throughout the year, but rainfall and wind vary seasonally. The generally drier period is **December to April**. Winds and waves can still be stronger on exposed Caribbean waters in these months, while calmer days also occur during the wetter season.

Canal transit follows its own operating rules and shipping schedule; subsequent island passages depend on the sea. **Weather in Panama City does not necessarily reflect conditions at Shelter Bay or San Blas.** Plan with forecasts for each stage and allow possible changes to the anchorage sequence for navigation safety.

On board, bring non-slip shoes, sun protection, lightweight clothes for island days, a windproof layer and a compact waterproof bag. Guests prone to seasickness should discuss it with a doctor beforehand: waves are possible even in otherwise pleasant weather. If you would rather explore different Panamanian regions without living aboard for several nights, compare other [Panama tours](/panama/tour/) and the [San Blas tours catalog](/panama/place/san-blas-islands/tour/).

## Frequently asked questions

### How many Ada Tours trips visit Shelter Bay?

We offer an eight-day yacht route. The live catalog determines the actual count and tour details, so the list may change when new programs are published.

### On which day does the yacht arrive at Shelter Bay?

In the [eight-day itinerary](/panama/tour/panama-san-blas-luxury-yacht/), Shelter Bay is scheduled for day two, after the yacht transits the canal from the Pacific to the Caribbean.

### Is a hotel stay at the marina included?

No confirmed hotel accommodation at Shelter Bay is specified. The program provides nights aboard the yacht. The marina stop is part of the sailing route, not a separate shore stay.

### Does the yacht tour include San Lorenzo Fortress?

No, a visit to [San Lorenzo Fortress](/panama/place/san-lorenzo-fort/) is not part of this yacht itinerary. Other [tours visiting the fortress](/panama/place/san-lorenzo-fort/tour/) are available.

### Which islands are visited after the bay?

The itinerary names [El Porvenir](/panama/place/el-porvenir-island/), [Coco Bandero](/panama/place/coco-bandero-island/), the [Holandes Cays](/panama/place/holandes-cays/), [Isla Perro](/panama/place/isla-perro/) and [Turtle Island](/panama/place/turtle-island/) in sequence. These are planned stops; the crew adjusts the actual sailing sequence to navigation conditions.

### How is a journey via Shelter Bay different from a beach holiday?

It begins with **transiting the Panama Canal**, then continues by yacht between islands. A conventional beach holiday often centers on staying in one location. On the Shelter Bay route, sailing, life aboard and several geographically distinct stops are part of the experience.
